    Mann Star-Stride¶

    [!INFO] One Stride Under the Same Stars — Mann Does Not Bend the Measure The pilgrim measure of the Mann Order — counted by footfall under Mann's own heavens. A theocratic mile that refuses to be Erisian.

    Base Units¶

    The Star-Stride is founded on the body and the heavens. Mann is capital of the gods — its measure is therefore correct, not merely convenient. The priests keep a basalt Stride-stone at the capital of Mann — a slab worn hollow by centuries of standard-setters pacing its length. The measure is re-drilled each winter solstice when the star Mann (the pole star of Ge'or's north) culminates over the temple gnomon.

    Domain Unit Relation Notes
    Length Finger base as Erisian — but Mann finger is broader
    Palm 4 Fingers
    Mann-Foot 12 Fingers 32.1 cm — longer than Erisian, longer than dwarven — Mann stature is the standard
    Stride 2.5 Mann-Feet 80.25 cm — single step of a Mann pilgrim in full stride
    Star-Stride 1,000 Strides the Star-Stride — 802.5 m. Distance walked while the star Mann moves 1 degree (by water-clock). Also 880 Erisian Yards
    Daymarch 32 Star-Strides 25.68 km — a pilgrim's day on good road. Mann to the frontier in twelve Daymarches
    Pilgrim League 3 Daymarches ~77 km — between shrines. Mann maps mark shrines, not towns
    Weight Grain base as Erisian
    Pennyweight 24 Grains star-iron assay — Meteor iron from Mann heights
    Ounce 20 Pennyweights
    Pound 16 Ounces 458 g — star-pound, heavier due to Mann-Foot chain
    Stone 14 Pounds 6.41 kg
    Volume Horn base drinking horn ~ 350 mL — vow horn
    Stoup 2 Horns
    Bucket 10 Stoups 7 L
    Barrel 6 Buckets 42 L — shrine barrel

    Mann catechism for children: Foot, Stride, Star, Day — walk as the star walks.

    The Erilian Federation calls the Star-Stride pagan arithmetic. Mann calls the Erisian Mile a southern yard stretched by vanity.

    Who Uses¶

    The Mann Order alone — zealously, exclusively, theocratically. Also among Mann refugees in New Mann (Fractured State of Erislod) who keep the Stride as identity. The order's legates refuse Erisian chains at border crossings and must be threaded — Mann priests unroll a 1-Star-Stride rope and count it themselves while Crown exchangers watch. Deliberately slow.

    Also used by Kosbaldo-loyal communities and Mannosta-star pilgrims. Some Cossiland border villages use Star-Strides informally — and deny it when the Crown asks.

    Conversion Notes¶

    • To Erisian Standard: 1 Mann-Foot = 1.053 Erisian Feet. 1 Stride = 2.63 Erisian Feet. 1 Star-Stride = 2,631 Erisian Feet = 0.498 Erisian Miles (≈ half a Mile). Mann maps compress: a Pilgrim League looks short on a Mann map and shocks Erisian quartermasters when it is not.
    • To Dwarven Stone: 1 Star-Stride = 28.66 Dwarven Stone. Dwarven merchants at the north road have a slate: 1 SS = 28 S + 18 Thumbs — pay accordingly.
    • To Vennerian/Anosi: No official conversion — Mann priests will not certify it. Field rule: 1 Star-Stride ≈ 4.33 Vennerian Cables. Vennerian pilots ignore the Star-Stride and charge in Cables; Mann pilgrims ignore the Cable and walk.
    • Non-convertible principle: Like the Mannic Star coin, the Star-Stride is deliberately non-convertible in law. In practice every border factor converts it at 1 Star-Stride = 0.88 Erisian Chains and charges the pilgrim for the math.
    • Romanium: Romanium is weighed in star-pounds for temple tithe, but Mann has almost no Romanium — the tithe is symbolic. One grain of Romanium dust is a star saved.

    Flavor¶

    Mann measure is refusal as piety. To measure as Mann measures is to declare we are not Erisdar's south. A Mann child is taught to pace the temple courtyard until his Stride matches the hollow in the Stride-stone — when it does, he is a man. A Mann funeral procession moves exactly one Star-Stride — no more, no less — while the star Mann is visible.

    Erisian surveyors brought Chains to Mann after the 585 AGD invasion. Mann peasants buried them. When Erilian factors re-measured in Miles, yields fell on paper and rose in the granary — the same field, counted differently. That, priests say, is why the star measure matters: it remembers whose feet walked the field.

    Motto at the border: Our Star, Our Stride — No Other.
